hints: Hint 1: Recall what quantity is obtained by multiplying velocity by time, since area = height x base on a velocity-time graph.
teacher_walkthrough: The definition of velocity is rate of change of displacement, so $v = \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$.
Rearranging gives $\Delta s = v \Delta t$, which corresponds to the area of a strip under the $v$ against $t$ graph.
Therefore the total area under the velocity-time graph represents displacement.
common_pitfalls: Stating distance instead of displacement, which loses precision because velocity is a vector.
Confusing gradient with area and stating acceleration.

hints: Hint 1: Identify the sloping section of the graph for trolley B in Fig. 3.2 as the collision period and read its start and end velocities and times.
Hint 2: Set up acceleration as gradient $a = (v-u)/(t_2-t_1)$ using the change in velocity divided by the duration of contact.
teacher_walkthrough: Acceleration equals the gradient of a velocity-time graph, $$a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$$

From Fig. 3.2, trolley B moves at constant $u = 0.12\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ until $t_1 = 0.15\,\mathrm{s}$, then velocity increases uniformly to $v = 0.30\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ at $t_2 = 0.35\,\mathrm{s}$.
Acceleration: $$a = \frac{0.18}{0.20} = 0.90\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$$ in the original direction of motion.
walkthrough: Mark scheme step 1: $a =$ gradient or $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$.
common_pitfalls: Using the whole 0 to 0.50 s time interval instead of the 0.15 s to 0.35 s collision duration.
Misreading the final velocity of B as 0.40 instead of 0.30 from the grid.

formulas_used: m_A u_A + m_B u_B = m_A v_A + m_B v_B
hints: Hint 1: Apply conservation of linear momentum for an elastic collision with negligible external forces, taking motion to the right as positive.
Hint 2: Substitute masses and speeds from Table 3.1 with final velocity of B as $0.30\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ from Fig. 3.2 to form $m_A u_A + m_B u_B = m_A v_A + m_B v_B$.
Hint 3: Solve algebraically for $v_A$ and interpret the sign to give direction relative to the initial motion.
teacher_walkthrough: Conservation of linear momentum applies because resistive forces are negligible, $$m_A u_A + m_B u_B = m_A v_A + m_B v_B$$
Final momentum of B from Fig. 3.2: $$p_{B}' = 0.75 \times 0.30 = 0.225\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$$
Magnitude is $0.060\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ and the negative sign shows direction is to the left, opposite to its initial velocity and opposite to the final velocity of B.
walkthrough: Mark scheme step 3: direction to the left or opposite to initial velocity.
common_pitfalls: Omitting direction and giving only speed, which loses the final B1 mark.
Using conservation of kinetic energy alone with squared terms, which increases arithmetic error risk.

hints: Hint 1: Recall trolley A moves at constant $0.48\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ before contact, so draw a horizontal line from $t = 0$ to the collision start at $t = 0.15\,\mathrm{s}$.
Hint 2: Recall trolley A moves at constant final velocity after separation, so draw a horizontal line at your answer from (b)(ii) from $t = 0.35\,\mathrm{s}$ to $t = 0.50\,\mathrm{s}$.
Hint 3: Join the two horizontal sections with a straight line during the 0.15 s to 0.35 s contact time to show uniform acceleration.
teacher_walkthrough: Before collision there is no resultant force, so velocity is constant. Draw a horizontal line at $v = 0.48\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 0.15\,\mathrm{s}$.
After collision there is no resultant force, so velocity is constant. Draw a horizontal line at $v = -0.06\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ from $t = 0.35\,\mathrm{s}$ to $t = 0.50\,\mathrm{s}$.

During collision the interaction force is taken as approximately constant, so velocity changes uniformly. Draw a straight sloping line joining $(0.15, 0.48)$ to $(0.35, -0.06)$, crossing the time axis as A reverses direction.
walkthrough: Mark scheme step 1: horizontal line from (0, 0.48) to (0.15, 0.48).
Mark scheme step 2: horizontal line from (0.35, -0.06) to (0.5, -0.06).
Mark scheme step 3: straight line between (0.15, 0.48) and (0.35, -0.06).
common_pitfalls: Drawing the collision as instantaneous vertical drop instead of a slope over 0.15 s to 0.35 s.
Keeping the final velocity of A positive or above zero, contradicting momentum conservation.
